Occupational therapy

How occupational therapy can help

Every child is different, so therapy is built around your child's strengths and your family's goals. These are some of the areas families come to us for support with.

Sensory processing

Supporting how your child takes in and responds to sights, sounds, textures, and movement so they can join in comfortably.

Fine motor & handwriting

Hand strength and control for writing, drawing, buttons, zippers, and utensils.

Self-care & daily routines

Growing independence with dressing, toileting, brushing teeth, and getting ready.

Feeding & mealtimes

Gentle support for picky eating and making meals feel more comfortable.

Emotional regulation

Noticing big feelings and building tools to feel safe and in control.

Motor planning & coordination

Coordinating the body for play, sports, balance, and everyday movement.

Attention & executive function

Focus, transitions, planning, and following multi-step routines.

Play & social connection

Joining in, sharing, and building friendships in ways that feel authentic.

Support for children with:AutismADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder)PDA (Persistent Drive for Autonomy)Developmental delaysDown syndromeSensory processing disorderDevelopmental coordination disorder (dyspraxia)

DIR Floortime

A relationship-based approach, woven into every session

DIR Floortime is a child-led approach that values, acknowledges, and builds upon three things. It promotes development and genuine connection in a way that feels meaningful to your child.

D

Developmental

We meet your child at their current developmental stage and build up from there, one meaningful step at a time.

I

Individual differences

We honor the unique way your child takes in, processes, and responds to the world around them.

R

Relationships

Real growth happens through warm, trusting relationships, so connection always comes first.

Cultivate Play weaves DIR Floortime into therapy with every child, and coaches parents to use it at home so connection and growth continue between sessions.

Learn more about DIR Floortime in Murfreesboro

Our approach

Gentle, playful, and built around your child

Every child develops at their own pace. Here's how we turn strengths-based, neurodiversity-affirming care into a plan your family can actually live with.

01

Free phone consult

A no-pressure call to talk about your child and see whether we're the right fit.

02

Play-based evaluation

A relaxed, child-led session to understand your child's strengths and where support helps.

03

A plan built on strengths

We set goals together, around your family's routines, priorities, and your child's interests.

04

Grow together

Ongoing sessions at home, in the community, in office, or via telehealth, with progress you can see.

Meet the team

Kind, credentialed, and on your side

A small, dedicated practice that treats your family like part of theirs.

Alyssa Engel

OTD, OTR/L, DIR-Proficient

Alyssa started Cultivate Play, PLLC in 2024 in response to a lack of neurodiversity-affirming providers in the Middle Tennessee area. She earned a B.S. in Exercise Science and her Occupational Therapy Doctorate (OTD) from the University of Tennessee, Chattanooga. She has experience across a variety of pediatric populations and specializes in neurodiversity-affirming, strengths-based care, including Autism, ADHD, and PDA (Persistent Drive for Autonomy). Alyssa is also neurodivergent (an ADHDer), so she understands first-hand many of the experiences of neurodivergent children and their families. A certified DIR Floortime provider, she is passionate about home and community-based care that supports authentic, meaningful participation. She lives in Murfreesboro and enjoys crafting, the outdoors, and traveling.

Valerie Navis

COTA/L

Valerie is passionate about helping children grow through play. She believes the best therapy happens when children feel seen, heard, and excited to play. She uses a child-led, play-based approach to meet each child where they are, turning their interests into opportunities for growth. Her goal is to create a supportive, fun environment where kids can build skills, confidence, and independence, and be themselves.

Child-led
